claims.claim_text: At approximately 0245 hours, dispatch received a 911 call from a named witness reporting subjects breaking into vehicles.
At approximately 0249 hours, I indicated I would respond along with K9 Officer Falk and Trainee Vega.
The vehicle's engine was off and no lights were visible.
I exited my patrol vehicle and approached the passenger side of the Escalade.
I immediately observed the subject in the driver's seat and a second individual in the rear passenger seat.
The subject responded clearly in English that he understood and would comply when he was ready. Body-worn cameras were activated from the outset of the contact.
K9 Officer Falk arrived approximately fifteen minutes after my initial contact with the subject.
The subject immediately became hostile, producing a black handgun from under his seat and waving it toward officers through the driver's side window.
A single 40mm OC round was deployed through the front windshield, which immediately caused the subject to cover his face and cease yelling.
The subject placed the vehicle in drive and accelerated straight forward through the gate at what I estimated to be approximately 45 miles per hour.
The entire sequence from initial acceleration to exit through the building took less than ten seconds.
I discharged my patrol rifle four rounds in approximately four seconds. Sergeant Ingram discharged his sidearm five rounds. Officer Navarro also discharged her sidearm three rounds.

Paramedics from Los Angeles County Fire Department arrived within two minutes of the shooting and transported the subject to a local hospital, where he was pronounced deceased approximately one hour later.
A loaded semi-automatic pistol was recovered from the subject's lap during the vehicle search.
The subject raised his right arm holding the previously observed handgun and pointed it directly at Sergeant Ingram.
